prompt.context_jp: 「京橋支店ってエリート店舗ですよね？」
prompt.prompt_jp: もう何年も業績表彰1位___続いてるな。

feedback.correct_en: The subject '業績表彰1位' is new information being asserted as what has been continuing — this is neutral-description が, reporting a fact.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize '1位' as already-known, which doesn't fit this fact-reporting tone. を doesn't work because 続く is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: As for the rain, it's falling. (contrastive/topic)

prompt.context_jp: 筋トレの話で。
prompt.prompt_jp: 芝崎次長 筋肉___裏切りませんから。

feedback.correct_en: '筋肉は裏切らない' is a generic saying — '筋肉' is the topic being characterized. は gives it the proverb-like flavor Souma intends.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like reporting a surprising fact about one specific instance, not a universal truth. を is wrong because 裏切る here takes the subject marker.

contrast_examples.en: HE was the one who betrayed. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 相馬の横顔を見て。
prompt.prompt_jp: その横顔には、舞がこれまであまり見たことのない、遠い日を思い出すような影___差していた。

feedback.correct_en: The 'shadow' is brand-new information appearing on Souma's face — neutral-description が introduces this newly-observed subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply '影' is already an established topic being contrasted, which doesn't fit this descriptive narrative moment. に is wrong grammatically for the subject.

contrast_examples.en: A shadow fell on his face. (new observation)

prompt.context_jp: 紀本が京橋支店員に訓示。
prompt.prompt_jp: 君たち___当行の誇りです。

feedback.correct_en: '君たち' is set up as the topic being characterized ('as for you all, you are our pride'). This is classic は-topic usage in a declarative statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like 'YOU (and not others) are the pride', an exhaustive identification that's not the speaker's intent here. も adds 'also', which has no basis in context.

contrast_examples.en: It's you who are our pride. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 行員の輪の中心を見ると。
prompt.prompt_jp: その中心にいるの___、仕立てのいいスーツに身を包んだ年配の男性だった。

feedback.correct_en: 'その中心にいるの' is the topic being described — は sets up the frame 'as for who's at the center', followed by the identifying description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-focus attention; the sentence is describing what the already-mentioned center contains. を is grammatically wrong here.

contrast_examples.en: The one at the center is him. (topic-comment)
At the center, there IS him. (existence, new info)

prompt.context_jp: フロアの張り詰めた空気について。
prompt.prompt_jp: 業績表彰一位の支店にしては、フロアの空気が妙に張り詰めているように舞___は感じられた。

feedback.correct_en: 感じられる (spontaneous/passive sense) marks the experiencer with に. '舞には' = 'to Mai, it felt...'
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks location or means, not the person experiencing a sensation. を doesn't fit intransitive 感じられる.

contrast_examples.jp: 私には難しく感じられる。

prompt.context_jp: 紀本の反応を見た後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞___、紀本の顔に一瞬浮かんだこわばりを見逃していなかった。

feedback.correct_en: Mai is the ongoing topic of the narrative — は continues her as theme while the comment reports what she noticed.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as new/exhaustive information, inappropriate when she's the established POV character. に doesn't fit the subject slot of 見逃していなかった.

prompt.context_jp: 二人が沈黙している場面で。
prompt.prompt_jp: 机の上の彼岸花だけ___、二人の沈黙の中で赤々と咲いていた。

feedback.correct_en: '〜だけが' marks exhaustive listing — only the spider lily, and nothing else, was blooming. The が emphasizes the exclusive subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は after だけ is possible but weaker; here the narrative wants the exhaustive 'only X, and X alone' feel, which が delivers.

prompt.context_jp: 昇仙峡について相馬が言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___紀本部長の懐刀だぞ。

feedback.correct_en: '彼女' is the topic being characterized — Souma states what she IS. は fits this declarative topic-comment structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mean 'SHE (not someone else) is the right-hand person', which isn't the discourse here. も adds 'also', not what's meant.

prompt.context_jp: 臨店の仕事について。
prompt.prompt_jp: どれほど小さなミスにも、それが起きた理由___必ずある。

feedback.correct_en: Existence sentences with ある introducing the thing that exists use が — '理由がある' asserts that a reason exists.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize 'reason' as something already in discussion, which doesn't fit this general assertion. を doesn't go with ある.

prompt.context_jp: 河合の夫が病院で。
prompt.prompt_jp: 妻___仕事が好きなんです。

feedback.correct_en: Classic double-subject pattern: '妻は' is the topic, '仕事が' is the thing-loved. は marks the whole-sentence topic, が marks the object of 好き.
feedback.incorrect_en: が for 妻 would make it a new-information/exhaustive subject, but here the husband is talking ABOUT his wife (topic). を doesn't pair with 好き.

contrast_examples.en: My wife chose the job. (actor + object)

prompt.context_jp: 相馬が銀行を評する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「結果が全て」それ___この銀行だ。

feedback.correct_en: 'それがこの銀行だ' identifies the just-stated motto AS the essence of the bank — exhaustive/identifying が, pointing back to the quoted phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'それ' a topic being described, weakening the pointed identification Souma intends. も doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: THAT is what this bank is. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 勤務表を見て相馬が。
prompt.prompt_jp: 融資課全員 時間外勤務___ゼロか。

feedback.correct_en: '時間外勤務' is the topic being characterized (as being zero). は sets up the frame and the comment 'ゼロか' comments on it.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark overtime as new information or exhaustive, but Souma is making a general observation about overtime status. を doesn't pair with the copula.

prompt.context_jp: オフィス街の描写。
prompt.prompt_jp: 秋の日差し___ビルのガラス窓に反射して、通りをまぶしく照らしている。

feedback.correct_en: Scenic description introducing the sunlight as a fresh observation — neutral-description が. The reader hasn't encountered this sunlight as topic yet.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the sunlight an established topic, out of place in this opening scenic image. を doesn't fit with 反射する.

contrast_examples.en: The wind is cold. (commenting on topic)

prompt.context_jp: 臨店班の立場について。
prompt.prompt_jp: 本部の人間が表彰の場___居合わせるのは、支店にとって決して歓迎されることではない。

feedback.correct_en: 居合わせる takes に to mark the place where one happens to be present. The particle marks the location of existence/presence.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the place of an action, but 居合わせる emphasizes being present AT a scene, which takes に. を doesn't fit this verb.

contrast_examples.en: I happened to be at the scene.
I worked at the scene. (action location)

prompt.context_jp: 相馬の内省。
prompt.prompt_jp: 銀行のために努力を惜しまない行員___ど、組織の都合でたやすくすり減らされていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the correct particle (after 行員).

feedback.correct_en: The pattern '〜ほど...' means 'the more X, the more Y'. The suffix ほど expresses proportionality with the harsh consequence that follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just mark a subject without the proportional meaning. を doesn't fit the clause structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 努力する人ほど報われる。
contrast_examples.en: The more you try, the more rewarded.

prompt.context_jp: 相馬が紀本に会ったことについて。
prompt.prompt_jp: まさか臨店先で紀本部長に___とはな。

feedback.correct_en: '〜に会う' is the collocation for meeting/encountering a person. Combined with 'まさか...とはな' it expresses surprise at the encounter.
feedback.incorrect_en: '見る' would describe mere sight, not an encounter. '聞く' doesn't fit a chance meeting.

contrast_examples.en: I saw a friend (from a distance).

prompt.context_jp: 支店長が紀本部長に誓う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 業績表彰トップの名に恥じぬよう ___ 努めてまいります！

feedback.correct_en: 粉骨砕身 (lit. 'pulverize bones, shatter body') is a formal set phrase for pledging utmost effort — fitting for this grandiose pledge.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一石二鳥 ('two birds one stone') is about efficiency. 自業自得 means 'you reap what you sow' — opposite nuance.

contrast_examples.en: I will give it my utmost.

prompt.context_jp: 紀本が彼岸花を見て。
prompt.prompt_jp: たちの悪い___だ。縁起の悪い花を送って私に不快な思いをさせたかったんだろう。

feedback.correct_en: 'たちの悪いいたずら' = 'a nasty prank' — Kimoto dismisses the flower as malicious mischief.
feedback.incorrect_en: お祝い (celebration) and 贈り物 (gift) wouldn't be modified by 'たちの悪い' (ill-natured) in this context.

prompt.context_jp: 清田課長の持論。
prompt.prompt_jp: 残業するヤツは仕事が___証拠。

feedback.correct_en: '仕事ができない' = 'can't do the job (well)' — a set phrase for incompetence. The manager uses it to blame overtime workers.
feedback.incorrect_en: '仕事をしない' means refusing to work, not inability. 'わからない' doesn't collocate with 仕事 in this evaluative sense.

prompt.context_jp: 紀本と川野の関係について。
prompt.prompt_jp: 理不尽なやり方に黙っていられない川野とは、いわば___だ。

feedback.correct_en: 水と油 ('water and oil') is the set phrase for things that fundamentally don't mix — perfect for describing Kimoto and Kawano.
feedback.incorrect_en: 犬猿の仲 means 'bitter enemies' but implies active hostility between known rivals. 一心同体 means 'one in body and mind' — the opposite.

contrast_examples.en: The two don't mix at all.

prompt.context_jp: 舞が残業未払いを批判する。
prompt.prompt_jp: だからって残業させておいて賃金は払わないなんて、___過ぎます。

feedback.correct_en: 'ブラック(企業)' is Japanese slang for exploitative workplaces. 'ブラック過ぎる' fits Mai's outrage at unpaid overtime.
feedback.incorrect_en: ホワイト企業 is the opposite (good workplace). グレー suggests ambiguity, too weak for Mai's strong criticism.

contrast_examples.jp: あの会社はブラックだ。
あの会社はホワイトだ。

prompt.context_jp: 相馬が黙り込んで。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞は何か言葉を探したが、相馬の沈黙にはどこか___ものがあった。

feedback.correct_en: 踏み込みがたい = 'hard to step into/intrude upon' — captures Mai's hesitation about Souma's heavy silence.
feedback.incorrect_en: わかりやすい (easy to understand) and にぎやかな (lively) contradict the contemplative, uneasy atmosphere.

prompt.context_jp: 行員の答えが皆同じ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰に聞いても、返ってくる答えは___ように同じだった。

feedback.correct_en: '判で押したよう' (as if stamped with a seal) is the idiom for identical/stereotyped responses — perfect for suspiciously uniform answers.
feedback.incorrect_en: 水を打ったよう describes dead silence (a crowd going hushed). 油を売る means 'slack off' — unrelated.

contrast_examples.jp: 判で押したような返事。
水を打ったような静けさ。
contrast_examples.en: A hush fell over the room.

prompt.context_jp: 中西支店長が紀本部長に事務ミスを釈明する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for a branch manager downplaying an issue to a superior?

choices.text: 問題というほどのことじゃないんです。ほんの小さな事務ミスがあっただけでして。
問題じゃないよ。ちょっとミスしただけだから。
問題あるかないかわからないけど、ミスはあった。

feedback.correct_en: The actual line uses hedging ('〜ほどのことじゃない', 'ほんの小さな', '〜でして') — all register-appropriate for deferential business speech to a superior.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is casual speech, inappropriate to a 部長. (c) is ambiguous/awkward and lacks politeness markers.

contrast_examples.jp: 問題というほどのことじゃないんです。
contrast_examples.en: It's nothing worth calling a problem (humble).

prompt.context_jp: 舞が青ざめた河合に声をかける。
prompt.prompt_en: Which is the most natural way for Mai to tell Kawai not to push herself?

choices.text: 体調がすぐれないようでしたら、無理しないでください。
体調が良くないなら、無理するな。
体が悪いので、無理しません。

feedback.correct_en: '〜ようでしたら' softens the condition, and '〜ないでください' is standard polite request — natural workplace empathy from Mai.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is blunt/male imperative, not Mai's style with a stranger. (c) is grammatically off — it describes Mai's own state.

contrast_examples.jp: 無理しないでください。

prompt.context_jp: 相馬が昇仙峡の生き方について。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for Souma's reflective statement that people have their own ways?

choices.text: 生き方は人それぞれ、いろいろだからな。
生き方が人ごとに、各種類あるから。
生きる方法は人ずつ、色々あるので。

feedback.correct_en: '人それぞれ' is the idiomatic way to say 'each person differs'. Combined with 'いろいろだからな' it sounds reflective and natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) and (c) use unidiomatic combinations like '人ごとに' with '各種類' or '人ずつ' that native speakers wouldn't use here.

contrast_examples.jp: 考え方は人それぞれだ。
contrast_examples.en: Everyone has their own way of thinking.

prompt.context_jp: 中西支店長が臨店班に待ってほしいと言う。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural for asking someone to wait because you're busy?

choices.text: ちょっと待っててくれるか、今それどころじゃないから。
少し待機するか、現在それの場合じゃないから。
ちょっと待っていてくださる、今はその時じゃないから。

feedback.correct_en: 'それどころじゃない' is the set phrase for 'this isn't the time for that'. Combined with the casual 'くれるか' it fits a manager speaking to subordinates.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) uses stilted vocabulary like 待機/現在 that don't match spoken register. (c) misuses くださる as a plain form and the latter phrase is unidiomatic.

contrast_examples.jp: 今それどころじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't have time for that right now.

prompt.context_jp: 舞が働くことの意味を問いかける。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best captures Mai's thoughtful, rhetorical question?

choices.text: 体や心をこわしてまで働くことに、何の意味があるんでしょうか。
体と心をこわしながら働くのは、意味ありますか。
体や心の故障まで労働に、どんな意味なのでしょうか。

feedback.correct_en: '〜してまで' = 'to the extent of doing X' expresses the extreme nature of the sacrifice. '何の意味があるんでしょうか' is a reflective rhetorical question.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) uses '〜ながら' which just means 'while', losing the 'to the point of' nuance. (c) uses unnatural noun combinations like 心の故障 and 労働.

contrast_examples.jp: 健康を損ねてまで働く。
contrast_examples.en: Work even at the cost of health.

contrast_examples.jp: 健康を損ねながら働く。
